about: The Field Cogitator Next track: designed but not yet built. Each item is a Proposal until the user approves it; implementation takes only Approved items. Same rules as the Battle Augur gallery (DEC-074 in the Battle Augur docs).

items.title: Direction A: Linear-first
items.summary: Entry editor as a dense grouped entry list beside a detail view with a properties panel; diagnostics are an inbox (D4 mood board).

items.title: Direction B: Notion-first
items.summary: Entry editor as a document page: properties block, statements as blocks and toggles, mentions with peek, / insert, backlinks; diagnostics as margin notes (D4 mood board).

items.title: Direction C: Augur blend
items.summary: Entry editor in Battle Augur desktop panes and tokens (tree with status edges and cost column, inspector), Linear speed (palette, issues inbox, keys) and the entry as a Notion-style page. Recommended (D4 mood board).

items.title: Direction D: User mix (A + B + C)
items.summary: Entry editor mixing the three directions: B's sidebar and document page in the middle; selecting a source opens A's dense grouped list beside the sidebar; a floating helper box (issues, suggestions, actions) collapses to a pill or expands into C's resizable inspector panel; focus mode (double-click a source, ⌘. or the toolbar) hides the sidebar. Interactive mock.
items.source: User mix of A, B and C (2026-11-22)

items.title: Design language (from Direction D)
items.summary: Direction D written down as one token file (src/language/tokens.css: semantic colour light and dark, type, spacing, density, radii, elevation, motion, focus) with a Windows platform layer, large text, forced colours and reduced motion, plus layout numbers and the collapse order (src/language/layout.ts). Direction D reads them; its captures are byte-identical. Gallery page ?page=language.

items.title: Elements view
items.summary: Every primitive Direction D uses, live from the tokens, in light and dark and on macOS and Windows where they differ, with states side by side; new: Windows window frame (caption buttons), command palette (⌘K), context menu, the large text rule for rows. Entries listed in cogitator.design.json (elements.sections). Gallery page ?page=elements.

items.title: E1 start window (recent datasets)
items.summary: What Field Cogitator shows with no dataset open: the app actions in the sidebar (Open folder…, Open file…, Convert from XML data…, the sample, Settings), recent datasets as dense rows with a status edge from the last check, a drop target; states recent, first run, opening (steps with counts and Cancel), missing on disk, 960 px and large text; macOS and Windows.

items.title: E1 open errors
items.summary: Dialogs (sheets on macOS) over the start window when a dataset cannot be opened as is: not a dataset (Convert… for XML data files), newer DKLPO version (open read-only), files that do not parse (open anyway, they open as source text with their errors), folder not writable (open read-only or Save as…). One sentence, the folder, choices as verbs; Return = primary, Esc = Cancel; macOS and Windows.

items.title: E1 window-level dialogs over the editor
items.summary: Over a static Direction D window: the dataset switcher popover (open dataset, recents, Open…, Convert…, Show in Finder, Close dataset), unsaved changes (Save / Don’t save / Cancel with the changed entries), a module changed on disk without and with unsaved edits (Reload / Keep mine / Compare), save failed (reason, Retry, Save as…). macOS.

items.title: E1 settings window
items.summary: Settings: macOS ~720 px window with toolbar tabs and the classic preferences layout; Windows: Windows settings layout (navigation list, section title, label + help left, control right) in the app frame, without setting cards. General, Editor, Checking, Text, Appearance, Keyboard (read-only shortcut list), Command line (engine and tool versions). No accounts, sync or cloud.

items.title: E1: Source text beside the page
items.summary: Source (⌘⌥U) splits the editor into the entry page and its DKLPO text, synced both ways; text editor with line numbers, syntax colours, diagnostic gutter and underlines, hover card, quick-fix menu (⌥↵) and status line; a module that doesn't parse opens as text only. States: split, text only, unknown reference, parse error, large text, 960 px.

items.title: E1: Go to definition, peek and backlinks
items.summary: Following references: Go to definition with Back / Forward and breadcrumbs, an inline peek (page or text, editable in place), backlinks as a fourth tab of the helper panel grouped by source and layer, and an unresolved reference that offers its fix instead of navigating.

items.title: E1: Diagnostics inbox
items.summary: The dataset's diagnostics as a full Linear-style inbox from the sidebar's Updates: grouped by kind, filter chips (source, layer, code), keyboard triage, a detail pane with the affected text or the export difference, bulk fix per suggestion code; out-of-date and no-issues states. The helper panel stays the quick view beside a page.

items.title: E1: Editor empty states
items.summary: Empty states inside the editor: a source with no entries (inline New entry with its key), an entry with no statements (the / hint as the first block), a search with no result (the palette says what it searched and offers next steps).

items.title: E1: Run checks
items.summary: Run checks (⌘⇧C) inside the editor: a check status button in the page toolbar (complete, n errors, doesn't compile, running, out of date) opens a run popover with the steps and counts (Parse, Compile, Lower, Export check) and Cancel, then the result per class with its codes leading into the diagnostics inbox, what was checked (dataset, profile, layers, patch, export dry run) and the same command to copy. States: running, complete, incomplete with counts, doesn't compile (stops before Lower), out of date.

items.title: E1: Convert from XML data
items.summary: Convert as a window of its own (from the start window and File › Convert…): the options in the left column as the convert command's flags in words (input folder / archive / files, output folder or Update, dataset key, version, text language, text columns, compatibility envelope, keep the original files, full id map, roundtrip after converting), the right pane with the input's documents, the steps with counts and Cancel, then the report (C2, C1, C3 verdicts, the numbers convert reports, each document's C1 differences, preservation diagnostics, Open the converted dataset, the commands to copy). Dry run writes nothing. States: options, converting, equal, differences found, input can't be read; macOS and Windows.

items.title: E1: Export
items.summary: Export (⇧⌘E) as a sheet over the editor: format (XML data files / JSON data files for documents added since conversion), destination, text language, and the exactness from a dry run as the sheet opens: exact (all envelope entries current, Write the original files available, C3) or not exact with counts and each reason (preserve/stale, preserve/unbound, preserve/original-outdated) and that it still writes (Export anyway) unless Require an exact export is on, which refuses and says why beside the button. Result lists the written files; a Level 1 construct refuses the export by name. States: exact, not exact, written, refused.

items.title: E1: Roundtrip
items.summary: Roundtrip as a tool view in place of the list and the page (like the inbox), with the two routes of the roundtrip command switched in the toolbar: from the XML data the dataset was converted from (C2 norm, C1 per-document source trees, the documents with verdicts) and from this dataset (deterministic writing, import and compare, reconvert with ids and files). Left: contracts and documents with status edges; right: what the selected row compared and every difference, with the command to copy. States: equal, differences, reverse route, refused (input partly imported).

items.title: E1: Rename with a move record
items.summary: Rename (F2) as a sheet over the editor: the new key with the module prefix and the move command's dry-run preview as you type: classification (parent-preserving, minor; structural, needs a new major with Raise the version as --bump-major), what rosters do on open (followed and listed as moved, or kept unresolved for review), counts, the records appended to moves.dkl (uses named after the entry get their own), every file's lines before and after; Apply writes all or none, ⌘Z undoes. A taken key refuses with move/new-exists. States: rename, move to another parent (structural, drawn ahead of move/relocate), conflict.

items.title: E1: Layer stack and page overlay
items.summary: The sidebar's Layers opens the dataset's layer stack: base, add-ons and variants in order (Derived or Explicit like --layers), kind, purpose, version, requires: result, applied or refused with the reason, patch report, values changed, conflicts (later wins) and the add-on display-only check; Show on page draws the layer overlay (changed values marked with their layer, effective beside base). States: stack OK, refused, conflict, add-on changes rules, entry page with overlay.

items.title: E1: Dataset search and replace
items.summary: ⇧⌘F searches entries, text, references and statements across sources and layers: results grouped by source and entry with highlights, kind / source / layer filters, a preview; Replace for names and text with a per-match preview; keys lead to Rename… (F2). States: results, no results, filters, replace preview.

items.title: E1: Dataset runner with hot reload
items.summary: User request 2026-11-23: Run (⌘R) builds a roster against the dataset in a basic developer UI, docked beside the editor or in its own window (960 px: takes the page area). What runs (dataset alone or with layers, variants, locale), Add list, roster tree, options / profile / rules, totals, engine errors; hot reload on save or while typing keeps the roster through the roster-open rules, with a change summary, the last good build on a compile error and a review of structural moves; Go to entry / Show in runner; Save as test scenario. States: empty, in progress, reloaded, compile error, kept for review, save as test, detached, 960 px.
